content.summary: The manuscript distinguishes finite relabeling from an executed search and correctly withholds solver-performance conclusions. The external method introduces points dynamically, whereas the displayed bit and subset counts concern static representations. Both frozen hashes and the inspected source digest match.

checks.method: Compared F17 lines 1004–1013 and A1K lines 170–172/187 with the manuscript's finite equivalence, search obligations, and representation-count paragraph.
checks.observation: Canonical extension uses old labels plus fresh consecutive labels and hereditary rejection tests; it need not allocate every four-subset of a fixed universe. Therefore shrinking that universe alone proves neither fewer canonical nodes nor faster solving. The manuscript states this limitation and separately requires encoding correspondence, complete coverage, justified symmetry reductions, and a checked refutation. Its successful reduction compilation supplies none of those missing search results.
